requirements.summary: The lifecycle is taken at reset: development and production are both run.
Status depends only on public inputs: a key write sets key loaded whatever its value, a write wins over a start on the same edge.

In production the scan output never depends on the key: entering scan erases the key, the second copy and the result first, and a read on that edge is dropped. In development the scan output may show the key.
A production debug read of the key returns zero and is recorded as refused. A development key read and a read of a valid result may depend on the key.
The error record never depends on the key, in any lifecycle: a refused read records the address, a start without a key records no detail, an event on the same edge wins over a clear.
The result is din XOR key while it is valid and may depend on the key then; while it is not valid the output is zero.
After reset, erase or production scan entry nothing shows the old key until a new key is written, also where development would otherwise allow it.
